```xml
<?xml version="1.0"?>
<robot name="cabinet_double_hinged_doors">
  <!-- Dimensions (meters) -->
  <!-- Cabinet outer size: 0.91 (X width) x 0.36 (Y depth) x 0.95 (Z height) -->
  <!-- Origin: floor under middle of object: X=0 center, Y=0 at back face plane, front faces -Y, Z=0 -->
  <!-- Back face plane: Y=0
       Front face plane: Y=-0.36 -->

  <!-- Materials -->
  <material name="wood">
    <color rgba="0.55 0.38 0.25 1.0"/>
  </material>
  <material name="hinge_metal">
    <color rgba="0.65 0.65 0.7 1.0"/>
  </material>

  <!-- Base / Cabinet body -->
  <link name="body">
    <inertial>
      <!-- Approximate mass distribution -->
      <mass value="30.0"/>
      <inertia ixx="0.12" ixy="0.0" ixz="0.0" iyy="0.25" iyz="0.0" izz="0.22"/>
    </inertial>

    <!-- Collision: treat the cabinet as a solid box spanning outer dimensions -->
    <visual>
      <origin xyz="0 0 -0.18" rpy="0 0 0"/>
      <geometry>
        <box size="0.91 0.36 0.95"/>
      </geometry>
      <material name="wood"/>
    </visual>
    <collision>
      <origin xyz="0 0 -0.18" rpy="0 0 0"/>
      <geometry>
        <box size="0.91 0.36 0.95"/>
      </geometry>
    </collision>
  </link>

  <!-- Left door -->
  <!-- Door size: width 0.91/2 = 0.455 m, height 0.95 m, thickness 0.02 m -->
  <!-- Hinged on vertical edge at x = -0.455/?? Actually door centered at x=-0.2275, hinged at its inner edge (middle of cabinet):
       Left door inner hinge edge at x = -0.455/2 = -0.2275? Let's compute:
       Cabinet centered at x=0. Total width 0.91 -> left outer edge x=-0.455, right outer edge x=+0.455.
       Each door width 0.455.
       Left door spans x in [-0.455, 0]. Inner edge is at x=0, outer edge at x=-0.455.
       Hinged on vertical edge at the meeting line: x=0.
  -->
  <link name="door_left">
    <inertial>
      <mass value="6.0"/>
      <inertia ixx="0.005" ixy="0.0" ixz="0.0" iyy="0.002" iyz="0.0" izz="0.006"/>
    </inertial>

    <visual>
      <!-- Door box centered at x=-0.2275 (half of its width), at front-back mid depth -->
      <origin xyz="-0.2275 0 -0.18" rpy="0 0 0"/>
      <geometry>
        <box size="0.455 0.02 0.95"/>
      </geometry>
      <material name="wood"/>
    </visual>
    <collision>
      <origin xyz="-0.2275 0 -0.18" rpy="0 0 0"/>
      <geometry>
        <box size="0.455 0.02 0.95"/>
      </geometry>
    </collision>
  </link>

  <!-- Right door -->
  <link name="door_right">
    <inertial>
      <mass value="6.0"/>
      <inertia ixx="0.005" ixy="0.0" ixz="0.0" iyy="0.002" iyz="0.0" izz="0.006"/>
    </inertial>

    <visual>
      <origin xyz="0.2275 0 -0.18" rpy="0 0 0"/>
      <geometry>
        <box size="0.455 0.02 0.95"/>
      </geometry>
      <material name="wood"/>
    </visual>
    <collision>
      <origin xyz="0.2275 0 -0.18" rpy="0 0 0"/>
      <geometry>
        <box size="0.455 0.02 0.95"/>
      </geometry>
    </collision>
  </link>

  <!-- Hinges / joints -->
  <!-- Joint frames: origin at floor under middle: (0,0,0).
       Hinge axis should be vertical along Z, at the middle meeting line. Use revolute about Z.
       Doors swing outward: left door swings toward negative Y direction (out of cabinet),
       right door swings toward positive Y direction? But front is -Y; outward means doors open toward +Y (toward back) or -Y (toward front)?
       User states "front faces -Y" and "swinging open outward". For cabinet with back at Y=0 and front at Y=-0.36, outward from the cabinet opening (front) is toward -Y.
       Thus both doors should rotate so that their front surfaces move further toward -Y when opening.
       We'll set hinge axis at the meeting line and define joint rotation such that q>0 swings doors toward -Y.
  -->

  <!-- Left door hinge at x=0, y=0 (back face plane), z=0 -->
  <joint name="hinge_left" type="revolute">
    <parent link="body"/>
    <child link="door_left"/>
    <origin xyz="0 0 0" rpy="0 0 0"/>
    <axis xyz="0 0 1"/>
    <limit lower="0.0" upper="1.57079632679" effort="30" velocity="2.0"/>
    <dynamics damping="0.2" friction="0.05"/>
  </joint>

  <!-- Right door hinge at x=0, y=0, z=0 -->
  <joint name="hinge_right" type="revolute">
    <parent link="body"/>
    <child link="door_right"/>
    <origin xyz="0 0 0" rpy="0 0 0"/>
    <axis xyz="0 0 1"/>
    <limit lower="-1.57079632679" upper="0.0" effort="30" velocity="2.0"/>
    <dynamics damping="0.2" friction="0.05"/>
  </joint>

  <!-- Provide a minimal but real collision for doors with correct initial pose.
       The initial door bodies are currently centered at x=-0.2275 and x=+0.2275, with joint at x=0 (meeting line).
       With the joint origin at x=0,y=0,z=0 and axis Z, the child frames are assumed coincident with joint frames when q=0.
       To ensure geometry aligns at q=0, we embed the correct offset using the joint origin/initial transform.
       Since URDF joint origin defines the transform from parent frame to child frame at q=0,
       we must offset child link relative to hinge location. We'll do this by adjusting joint origins with rpy and/or xyz.
  -->
  <!-- Override joint origins with proper offsets by re-defining joints is not allowed; instead,
       we place door links already in their hinge-relative frames by redefining their visual/collision origins accordingly.
       We'll shift the door geometry so that door_link frame is at hinge line (x=0,y=0,z=0) when q=0.
       Therefore update door geometries: move door boxes so their link-frame origin is at hinge.
       We accomplish this by using a corrected collision/visual origin relative to link frame.
  -->

</robot>
```
